title: 電気回路Ⅰ(再履修クラス)
subtitle: Electric Circuits I
keywords: AC circuits 2.Sine wave AC 3.Average and RMS values 4.Phasor representation 5.Region cooperation
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn the fundamentals of electric circuits consisting of resistance (R), inductance (L), capacitance (C), and their combinations connected to an AC power source. In addition, students will learn about phasor representation of sinusoidal AC.
advice: Below is an outline of the topics to be covered: AC circuit basics: properties of sine wave AC, effects of resistance, inductance, and capacitance, average and RMS values, phasor indication of sinusoidal AC This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit II, and Electrical Circuit III), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a basic course requirement. Based on the level of student understanding as indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and course content.
books: Basic electric circuit (2nd edition) New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: It is important that you solve as many problems as possible in order to understand and practice the theory presented. In addition, continuous effort is required on a daily basis. We encourage you to 1) examine various reference books, 2) ask the lecturer questions, and 3) take advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center so that you can clarify what you don't understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can draw and explain the waveform of a sine wave alternating current.
Participants can formulate the circuit equations for AC circuits consisting of R, L, and C.
Participants can calculate average and rms values of sine wave AC.
Participants can represent the phasor of sine wave AC.

achievementLevels.ideal: Participants can correctly draw and sufficiently explain the waveform of a sine wave AC and be able to correctly formulate the circuit equations of a sine wave AC circuit consisting of R, L, and C. They can correctly calculate the average and RMS values of a sine wave AC and sufficiently explain the physical meaning of the RMS value. They can represent correctly the phasor of a sine wave AC and sufficiently explain why complex numbers are introduced in the calculation of sine wave AC circuits.
achievementLevels.standard: Participants can draw and explain the waveform of a sine wave AC, and formulate the circuit equations of a sine wave AC circuit consisting of R, L, and C. They can calculate the average and RMS values of a sine wave AC and explain the physical meaning of the RMS value. They can represent the phasor of a sine wave AC and explain why complex numbers are introduced in the calculation of sine wave AC circuits.

lessons.content: Chapter 1 Circuit Elements 1.2 Element voltage and current 1.3 Element energy Chapter 5 Sine-wave AC circuit 5.1 Circuit equation
lessons.operation: Lecture, practice, and questions. In principle, subtests are conducted as many times as is appropriate with advance notice. The test is explained appropriately.
lessons.assignments: Read the sections of the textbook indicated in the left column. Review the matters learned that day. Write the correct answers for the tests. Be sure to submit your report by the deadline. Review the lecture and learn more about the circuit elements and circuit equations of a sine wave AC. Study textbooks to understand sinusoidal voltage and current.

lessons.content: Chapter 5 Sine wave AC circuit 5.2 Sinusoidal voltage, sinusoidal current
lessons.assignments: Review the lecture and deepen your understanding of sinusoidal voltage and current. Study textbooks to understand circuit equations for a single element.

lessons.content: Chapter 5 Sine wave AC circuit 5.3 Circuit equations for a single element
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of circuit equations for a single element. Study textbooks to understand circuit equations for multiple elements.

lessons.content: Chapter 5 Sine wave AC circuit 5.4 Circuit equations for multiple elements
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of circuit equations for multiple elements. Study textbooks to understand the power and power factor of sine wave AC circuits.

lessons.content: Chapter 5 Sine wave AC circuit 5.5 Power and power factor
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the power and power factor of sine wave AC circuits.

lessons.content: Exercises on basic circuits of sine wave AC.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of basic sine wave AC circuits. Study textbooks to understand the average and RMS values of periodic waveforms.

lessons.content: Chapter 6 Average and RMS values of periodic waveform 6.1 Average value 6.2 RMS value
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the average and RMS values of periodic waveforms. Study textbooks to understand the representation of sinusoidal functions in phasor form.

lessons.content: Chapter 7 Phasor representation of sine wave AC 7.1 Representation of sinusoidal functions in phasor form
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the representation of sinusoidal functions in phasor form. Study textbooks to understand complex numbers, conjugate complex numbers and phasor rotation.

lessons.content: Chapter 7 Phasor representation of sine wave AC 7.2 Complex numbers 7.3 Phasor in exponential form
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of complex numbers, conjugate complex numbers and the phasor rotation. Study textbooks to understand the differentiation and integration of sinusoidal functions.

lessons.content: Chapter 7 Phasor representation of sine wave AC 7.4 Differentiation and integration of sinusoidal functions
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the differentiation and integration of sinusoidal functions.

lessons.content: Preparation for “Electric Circuit II” (Analysis of sine wave AC circuits using the symbolic method)
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the analysis of sine wave AC circuits using the symbolic method.

lessons.operation: The exam covers the content of all lectures.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture and exercise questions that were not fully answered in the final exam.

lessons.content: Integrated learning of this course, Self-evaluation
lessons.operation: Return the final exam and explain the questions and answers. Clear unmet action goals identified in previous tests.
lessons.assignments: Self-check and try to resolve any lack of understanding of the previous practices and test questions.
